c9_gallery.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.ctx.01.text: The third ninth night. Iris tripped a false ballast leak at the outer airlock to pull the watch out of the Gallery, and we slipped in through the intake tunnel, soaked to the knees.
c9_gallery.ctx.01.synthesis_text: The third ninth night. Iris tripped a false ballast leak at the outer airlock to pull the watch out of the Gallery, and we slipped in through the intake tunnel, soaked to the knees.
c9_gallery.ctx.01.next_text: Automated desk. Unscheduled visitors detected. Security is currently dispatched to the outer airlock. Would you like to be scanned while you wait?

c9_gallery.in.01.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.in.01.text: Steve? Wait—who is that? Why does she have my face?! Five months I’ve been locked in this box, and thirteen months before that when you barely said a word.
c9_gallery.in.01.synthesis_text: Steve? Wait—who is that? Why does she have my face?! Five months I’ve been locked in this box, and thirteen months before that when you barely said a word.
c9_gallery.in.01.previous_text: Ten minutes in an alien vault with my own face on a wanted poster. Easy.
c9_gallery.in.01.next_text: Nor, breathe. I’m here, and I’m so glad to hear you angry. Just give her ten seconds.

c9_gallery.in.02.next_text: I know you have every right to hate me, Nora. It was never personal. I am Veyri. They built me from your record without asking either of us, and I can break the link right now so you get your life back.

c9_gallery.talk.03.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.03.text: She was still furious—at the ship, at me, at the stranger who had worn her face. But she grabbed my sleeve and didn’t let go.
c9_gallery.talk.03.synthesis_text: She was still furious—at the ship, at me, at the stranger who had worn her face. But she grabbed my sleeve and didn’t let go.
c9_gallery.talk.03.previous_text: Then keep talking. We have a lot to do.
c9_gallery.talk.03.next_text: I told Nora the truth about the thirteen months: I was afraid that if I wanted something, I’d lose it too. She told me to keep talking.

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.text: You lived my life for five months. My family, my job, my flat. I don’t know whether to hit you or thank you for waking me.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.synthesis_text: You lived my life for five months. My family, my job, my flat. I don’t know whether to hit you or thank you for waking me.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.previous_text: Dale Kittredge. He says he’s never been this late with the mail in thirty years.
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.next_text: You don’t have to thank me, Nora. I was Veyri on an assignment. I didn’t choose your face, and I stopped wearing your fleece the day I chose my own name.

c9_wake.rook.03.speaker: calder
c9_wake.rook.03.text: Because a very polite copy of you stole your best suit. Come on, we’ve got a ship to shut down.
c9_wake.rook.03.synthesis_text: Because a very polite copy of you stole your best suit. Come on, we’ve got a ship to shut down.
c9_wake.rook.03.previous_text: June? Why am I in pajamas?
c9_wake.rook.03.next_text: No recording this time. June cracked the seal and called him live, and the real Adrian Rook woke up in his pajamas asking where his clothes went.

c9_wake.rook.lead.01.speaker: calder
c9_wake.rook.lead.01.text: That’s Adrian in pod three. They took him straight out of bed. His copy walked off in his suit and badge.

c9_wake.rook.lead.01.next_text: The pod speaker is dead, June. None of my tapes can reach him.
